page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-16 is a virtual instance built on the x86_64 processor architecture within the general-purpose class. It allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no bundled hardware accelerators or GPUs, and local storage is listed as None, necessitating the use of remote persistent disk volumes for operating systems and runtime data.

The 1:2 memory-to-core configuration targets tasks that prioritize parallel execution throughput over high per-core memory capacity. By provisioning a lean memory tier relative to its 16 processing threads, it eliminates the cost overhead associated with unused memory in compute-dense scenarios. However, the absence of local NVMe storage and integrated public IPv4 addresses means system architects must plan for network-attached storage throughput and network egress requirements.

Workloads suited for this server configuration include continuous integration and build automation runners, stateless web serving fleets, media transcoding, data transformation tasks, and distributed batch processing nodes where working datasets fit comfortably inside 32 GB of operational memory.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 virtual compute instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The machine type includes no integrated graphics processors or local storage volumes, requiring external persistent storage attachments for operating system installation and scratch space. Networking configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because of its compute-skewed resource profile, this server avoids the expense of surplus memory capacity while providing substantial multi-threaded processing density. The machine is suited for compute-bound operations that operate with moderate memory requirements, including software build environments, batch processing jobs, API application tiers, and distributed data processing pipelines.
